I like to see what new projects people are working on in open-source, but I found it hard to find projects or news in any systematic way. I built Shadowgraph so that I could browse the latest in open source development in a more natural way. It ingests repos from github and scrapes hackernews, reddit, and X for mentions of them. I also identify noteworthy contributors on github and track what they're starring as a signal for potentially high quality projects that might otherwise fly under the radar. I also track their tweets or hackernews contributions for mentions of github repos for a more curated feed of content.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Cppbolt – A lightweight C++ to WebAssembly compiler written in Rust
show_hn.story_text:
Hey HN! I've been working on cppbolt, a lightweight C++ to WebAssembly compiler written in Rust. The idea was to build something that can compile and run C++ directly in the browser without downloading a massive LLVM/Clang toolchain. Unlike projects that bundle LLVM/Clang and can require 100+ MB of compiler assets, cppbolt's compiler payload is around 1 MB. It compiles a supported subset of C++17 directly to standard WebAssembly binaries. Some things it supports:
- Classes, inheritance, virtual functions and operator overloading
- Templates and a subset of the C++ standard library
- Pointers, references, arrays and dynamic memory
- Lambdas, structured bindings and range-based loops It comes with a browser playground, CLI and npm package. A few caveats: this is still a w
